metadata.name: Renal or ureteric stone
metadata.emergency_level: Urgent; emergency if infection plus obstruction, anuria, AKI or uncontrolled symptoms
metadata.severity: Ranges from self-limited colic to organ-threatening infected obstruction

overview.short_description: A mineral stone in the kidney or ureter that may cause sudden severe loin-to-groin colic, haematuria, obstruction or infection.
overview.detailed_description: Suspected renal colic requires timely imaging appropriate to age and pregnancy, effective analgesia, and immediate exclusion of infected obstruction. Stone size/site and patient factors determine observation, expulsive therapy or intervention; recurrence prevention follows stone/metabolic assessment.
overview.pathophysiology: Urinary supersaturation, crystal nucleation and growth produce stones that may obstruct the ureter, causing pressure, spasm and pain; obstruction with infection threatens renal function and life.
overview.etiology: Calcium, uric acid, infection-related, cystine and other stones; contributors include low urine volume, metabolic disease, infection, anatomy, diet and medicines.
overview.natural_history: Small stones may pass; others persist, recur, obstruct or become infected.
overview.prognosis: Good with appropriate analgesia and passage/removal; recurrence is common enough to justify prevention assessment.

incidence.value: Varies with climate, hydration, diet, metabolic and genetic factors

mortality.value: Very low without infection; infected obstruction can be fatal

epidemiology.age_groups: Mostly adults but occurs in children
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; hot climates may increase dehydration-related risk
epidemiology.seasonal_pattern: Heat/dehydration may increase presentations but is not diagnostic

risk_factors.lifestyle: Low urine volume, high salt intake and selected dietary patterns
risk_factors.occupation: Heat exposure or limited fluid/toilet access
risk_factors.family_history: Raises suspicion for recurrent/metabolic stone disease
risk_factors.medications: Selected drugs can crystallise or alter stone chemistry
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Prior stone, gout, hyperparathyroidism, bowel/malabsorption disease, recurrent UTI or urinary anomaly

chief_complaints.complaint: Sudden severe one-sided flank pain radiating toward groin
Nausea/vomiting and inability to keep still
Visible or microscopic blood in urine
chief_complaints.importance: Supportive but absence does not exclude

negative_findings.finding: No colicky flank pain and a comfortable still patient
negative_findings.why_important: Makes classic renal colic less likely

negative_findings.finding: No fever/rigors and stable renal function/urine output

history_questions.question: Did severe pain start suddenly in the side and move toward the groin?
Any fever, shaking, burning urine or feeling very unwell?
Can you pass urine; do you have one kidney, a transplant or known kidney disease?
Could you be pregnant, and what is the age?
Prior stones, stone analysis, gout, bowel disease, recurrent UTI, family history or stone-forming medicines?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Usually afebrile/stable; fever or instability is a red flag

physical_examination.examination: Hydration, urine output and genital examination if torsion is plausible

vital_signs.heart_rate: May rise with pain; persistent tachycardia requires reassessment
vital_signs.blood_pressure: Usually normal; hypotension is a red flag
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: Usually normal; elevation may indicate sepsis/pain
vital_signs.bmi: Record when relevant to risk or treatment

laboratory_tests.test_name: Urinalysis and urine culture when infection suspected
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: Assess obstruction, AKI and medicine safety
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: If infection or alternate inflammatory diagnosis suspected
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Identifies selected causes and stone type
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

imaging.imaging_type: Low-dose non-contrast CT within the urgent pathway for adults
imaging.when_needed: Suspected adult renal colic; ultrasound instead in pregnancy
imaging.expected_findings: Stone site/size, obstruction and alternate diagnosis
Hydronephrosis and some stones; CT considered if uncertainty remains

ecg.when_needed: Not routine; use when cardiac disease, electrolyte disturbance or medicine risk indicates

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Compatible renal-colic history plus guideline-appropriate imaging demonstrating renal/ureteric stone and obstruction status; assess infection and renal function concurrently.

diagnostic_scores.value: No single clinical score replaces imaging and emergency-risk assessment.

diagnostic_criteria.cutoff_values: Stone-size thresholds guide management in NG118; use current imaging report and guideline rather than copied standalone numbers.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Fever/systemic infectious syndrome rather than colic
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Fever/systemic infectious syndrome rather than colic

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there fever/rigors or reduced urine with suspected stone?
Is the patient pregnant or under 16?

next_best_question.question: Any fever/rigors, anuria/reduced urine, one kidney/transplant, pregnancy, uncontrolled pain/vomiting or anticoagulation?
next_best_question.branching_logic: High-risk -> urgent hospital/urology; otherwise analgesia and imaging pathway

next_best_test.why: Confirms site/size and obstruction and detects alternatives
next_best_test.expected_outcome: Observation, expulsive therapy or intervention decision

next_best_test.test: Urinalysis, culture if infected, and renal function

red_flags.finding: Suspected infected obstruction: fever/rigors or sepsis with an obstructing stone
Anuria, AKI, bilateral obstruction, solitary/transplanted kidney
Pregnancy with severe pain/obstruction or diagnostic uncertainty

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Persistent uncontrolled symptoms, obstruction, renal impairment, pregnancy complexity or stone unlikely to pass.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Recurrent stones, metabolic abnormality or asymptomatic stone requiring surveillance decision.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Infected obstruction/sepsis, anuria, AKI, bilateral/solitary-kidney obstruction.

late: Chronic renal damage in repeated/untreated obstruction

initial_management.supportive_care: Rapid analgesia, urine/renal assessment, appropriate imaging and emergency exclusion.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): NSAID; Intravenous paracetamol; Short-course opioid; Alpha blocker; Potassium citrate or thiazide prevention strategy. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG118_2026.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: After acute care, normal hydration and tailored dietary prevention; avoid extreme unsupervised restriction.
initial_management.follow_up: Confirm passage/removal where indicated and arrange stone/metabolic assessment for recurrence risk.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: NSAID first-line when suitable; IV paracetamol then opioid rescue if required; selected alpha blocker; prevention only after stone assessment.

patient_education.home_advice: Kidney stones can cause severe wave-like side pain. Fever or shaking with a stone, inability to urinate, one kidney, faintness or uncontrolled pain/vomiting are emergencies.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: قد تسبب حصاة الكلى ألماً شديداً متقطعاً في الخاصرة. وجود الحمى أو الرجفة مع الحصاة، أو انقطاع البول، أو وجود كلية واحدة، أو الإغماء، أو ألم/قيء غير مسيطر عليه هو حالة طارئة.
patient_education.prevention: Stone analysis, adequate fluids and cause-specific dietary/medical prevention.
patient_education.warning_signs: Fever, very low/no urine, worsening illness, one kidney, persistent vomiting or uncontrolled pain.

prevention.lifestyle: Adequate fluid intake and guideline-directed salt/diet advice
prevention.screening: Stone analysis and selected metabolic testing; serum calcium in adults

evidence.evidence_level: Guideline-grounded direction; no claim that every narrative sentence has clinician verification.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG118_2026; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Relieve renal colic, identify an infected obstructed kidney, image appropriately and prevent recurrence based on stone and metabolic assessment.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): NSAID; Intravenous paracetamol; Short-course opioid; Alpha blocker; Potassium citrate or thiazide prevention strategy. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG118_2026.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Strain urine when advised, maintain normal hydration after the acute episode, analyse retrieved stone, and tailor diet/fluids to recurrence assessment rather than extreme restriction.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Suspected renal colic when renal/GI/cardiovascular/pregnancy risks permit
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: chronic kidney disease, heart failure, hypertension, anticoagulation/antiplatelet therapy, older age, pregnancy, or dehydration
monitoring: renal function, blood pressure, oedema and gastrointestinal bleeding symptoms when clinically indicated
